title: 月下独酌·其二（天若不爱酒）
titleEn: Drinking Alone under the Moon, No. 2
author: 李白
intro: Li Bai builds a mock-serious argument for drinking: heaven has a Wine Star, earth has a Wine Spring, so loving wine must be perfectly proper. Funny, clever and a little lonely.
analysis: 李白的《月下独酌》共四首，第一首“举杯邀明月”最有名，这是第二首。这首诗像在“讲道理”，其实是开玩笑：天上有一颗“酒星”，说明天爱酒；地上有个地方叫“酒泉”，说明地也爱酒；既然天地都爱酒，我爱酒当然不用惭愧。接着用了一个典故：三国时曹操禁酒，喝酒的人偷偷把清酒叫“圣人”、浊酒叫“贤人”。李白说，圣人贤人我都“喝”进肚子里了，还求什么神仙？三杯下去就懂了天地大道，一斗下去就和自然融为一体。最后两句说：只要自己体会到酒中的乐趣就好，不必讲给清醒的人听——他们不会懂。整首诗用一本正经的推理写出一种狂放和幽默，背后却藏着一点孤独：能懂他的人太少了。
analysisEn: Li Bai wrote four poems called “Drinking Alone under the Moon”; the first, where he invites the moon to drink with him, is the famous one. This second poem is a playful, mock-serious argument. Heaven has a star called the Wine Star, so heaven must love wine; earth has a place called Wine Spring (Jiuquan, a real town in the northwest), so earth loves wine too. If heaven and earth both love it, why should he feel ashamed? Then he brings in an old story. When the warlord Cao Cao banned alcohol in the third century, drinkers secretly called clear wine “the sage” and cloudy wine “the worthy man”. Li Bai says he has drunk both the sage and the worthy, so what need does he have for immortals? Three cups and he understands the Great Way; a whole jug and he melts into Nature — a joking nod to Daoist ideas. The ending is the sharpest line: just enjoy the pleasure of wine, and don’t try to explain it to the sober, because they will never get it. Under the humour there is loneliness. The poem is called “drinking alone” for a reason: the people who could understand him are few.
background: Li Bai (701–762), the “Immortal of Poetry”, was famous for his love of wine and freedom. The four “Drinking Alone under the Moon” poems are traditionally dated to around 744, when he was in Chang’an and growing disappointed with court life.
pronunciation: 应 yīng（应该）。复道 fù dào。斗 dǒu（酒器、容量单位）。为 wèi（对、向）。传 chuán。机器朗读已把“应”“斗”“为”替换为同音字。
version: 采用通行文本（《李太白全集》）。“但得酒中趣”有的版本作“但得醉中趣”；“勿为醒者传”有的版本作“勿为醒者言”。

lines.lit: If heaven did not love wine,
lines.en: If heaven had no love for wine,

lines.lit: the Wine Star would not be in the sky.
lines.en: there’d be no Wine Star in the sky.

lines.lit: If earth did not love wine,
lines.en: If earth had no love for wine,

lines.lit: earth should have no Wine Spring.
lines.en: there’d be no Wine Spring on the ground.

lines.lit: Since heaven and earth both love wine,
lines.en: Since heaven and earth both love it,

lines.lit: loving wine, one need not be ashamed before heaven.
lines.en: why should I blush to love it too?

lines.lit: I have heard clear wine is compared to a sage,
lines.en: They say clear wine is like a sage,

lines.lit: and it is also said cloudy wine is like a worthy man.
lines.en: and cloudy wine is like a wise man.

lines.lit: Since I have already drunk the worthy and the sage,
lines.en: With sage and wise man both inside me,

lines.lit: why must I seek gods and immortals?
lines.en: what need have I to chase immortals?

lines.lit: Three cups, and I reach the Great Way;
lines.en: Three cups, and I see into the Way;

lines.lit: one dou, and I become one with Nature.
lines.en: a whole jug, and I’m one with Nature.

lines.lit: Only gain the delight within wine,
lines.en: Just enjoy the pleasure in the cup,

lines.lit: and do not pass it on to the sober.
lines.en: and don’t explain it to the sober.

words.note: 传说那里的泉水味道像酒，今天仍叫酒泉市。
古义“不感到惭愧”；今天“不愧”多表示“当得起”，如“不愧是冠军”。
古义“听到”，今天多指“用鼻子闻”。
这里指浊酒，未过滤的米酒。
这里是清酒、浊酒的代称。
道家所说的天地根本道理。
古义“只”，和今天的“但是”不同。

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 酒是全诗的主角：喝酒是快乐，也是与天地、自然相通的方式。
imagery.en: Wine is the star of the poem — a pleasure, and a way to feel at one with heaven, earth and Nature.

imagery.name: 天地
imagery.zh: 天上有酒星、地上有酒泉，诗人拉天地来为自己爱酒作证。
imagery.en: Heaven’s Wine Star and earth’s Wine Spring are called in as witnesses for his love of wine.

imagery.name: 星
imagery.zh: “酒星”在天，是诗人开玩笑的“证据”。
imagery.en: The Wine Star in the sky is his tongue-in-cheek “proof”.
